content.title: Standley Lake Library Trailhead Project
content.summary: The Standley Lake Library Trailhead was officially opened on November 15, 2024, in collaboration with the Jefferson County Public Library, enhancing community access to the Rocky Mountain Greenway. This trailhead features ADA-accessible routes, a central gathering area, picnic tables, and educational displays, benefiting local library patrons and over 3,500 students from nearby schools. The project was funded in part by a grant from Jeffco Open Space and aims to connect the community to regional trails and natural resources.
content.body:
![Aerial view of the Standley Lake Library Trailhead ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentID=4743 "Aerial view of the Standley Lake Library Trailhead ")

## Project Overview

On Nov. 15, 2024, in partnership with the Jefferson County Public Library (JCPL), the City of Arvada officially opened the Standley Lake Library Trailhead. Public remarks were made during a ceremonial ribbon cutting by the City of Arvada's Director of Vibrant Community and Neighborhoods Ryan Stevenson; Mayor Pro Tem Randy Moorman; JCPL Board of Trustee Jill Fellman and Senior Landscape Architect Chad Hollingsworth. Construction on the project began in March 2024.

The new trailhead provides the community with improved access to the [Rocky Mountain Greenway (RMG)](https://www.jeffco.us/3639/Rocky-Mountain-Greenway) and surrounding public trails. The RMG is a regional network of trails that connect the three National Wildlife Refuges in the Front Range – Rocky Mountain Arsenal in Commerce City, Two Ponds in Arvada and Rocky Flats in northwest Arvada/Superior. The vision of the RMG is to eventually provide trail connections to Rocky Mountain National Park.

The Standley Lake Library Trailhead creates the first trailhead in Arvada that directly connects to the RMG. The trailhead was funded in part by a 2021 Trails Partnership Program grant from Jeffco Open Space.

Watch videos of the trailhead on [YouTube](https://youtu.be/eHBBECyN_z4?feature=shared) and [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DCaNwnkyD9M/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==)

## Trailhead Features

The trailhead, located just west of the Standley Lake Library (8485 Kipling St.), features multiple ADA-accessible paved routes, linking the library parking lot and Kipling Street to the central trailhead and the RMG.

Designed with inclusivity and community in mind, the trailhead's amenities include:

- Central gathering area with bike racks, a shade shelter and covered seating
- Multiple new 8-foot-wide paved accessible trail routes from the library parking lot and Kipling Street to a central trailhead and to the existing RMG
- Half of the site's picnic and outdoor tables are designed to be wheelchair compatible
- Spaces throughout the site designed to serve as an outdoor classroom for the library's young readers
- Interpretive displays that describe Arvada's water sources and the importance of water throughout the City's history
- Xeric plantings and native plants – view a plant list for the trailhead site

In addition to serving outdoor enthusiasts, the trailhead will benefit local library patrons and more than 3,500 students from six schools within a 1.5-mile radius. A study done prior to the trailhead's construction identified trail-user groups as pedestrians (including walking, running, and wheelchair), recreational bicyclists, and school, work, or other utilitarian-purposed bicyclists, ranging in age from youth to seniors in Arvada and Westminster.

The trailhead serves the general community, library patrons, and more than 3,500 youth enrolled in six schools within a 1.5-mile radius.

The existing irrigation system was upgraded to effectively water the new landscape and restored areas.

## Project Timeline

- July 2022: Trail design options available:
- July 8 through August 1, 2022: Community engagement through Speak Up Arvada
- Fall and Winter 2022: Design concept refinement
- Fall 2023: Final City approval plans
- December 2023: Bid advertisement of construction project
- Spring 2024: Construction begins
- Fall 2024: Project completed
